sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的现场对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费阅读权限，畅享我们所有的深度报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: Over the past few days, social media companies have raced to remove the president and those who organized the attack on the Capitol from their platforMs.
sentences.zh: 过去几天里，社交媒体公司纷纷采取行动，将总统以及那些组织国会大厦袭击事件的人从其平台上移除。

sentences.en: My colleague, Shira Frankel, on whether that will diminish the chance of violence or make it harder to prevent.
sentences.zh: 我的同事希拉·弗兰克尔将探讨此举是会降低暴力风险，还是会让预防工作变得更加困难。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月13日，星期三。

sentences.en: Shira, last time that we talked to you, you told us about how supporters of President Trump were preparing and planning online in very knowable ways
sentences.zh: 希拉，上次我们采访你时，你提到特朗普总统的支持者们是如何以非常公开的方式进行准备和策划的，

sentences.en: for what became a violent attack on the Capitol on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 最终导致了1月6日那场针对国会大厦的暴力袭击。

sentences.en: And so I want to ask you what's happened to those same people in the days since and whether we now feel that the risk of future violence is higher or lower than before.
sentences.zh: 所以我想问你，在随后的几天里，这些人发生了什么？我们现在是否觉得未来发生暴力的风险比以前更高或更低了？

sentences.en: So the same people that took part in those riots on January 6th are now trying to find their footing in this new world.
sentences.zh: 参与1月6日骚乱的同一批人，现在正试图在这个新世界中寻找立足点。

sentences.en: What happens when a group of people do what really they thought was impossible and breach the halls of Congress, make it inside, hold court there for hours,
sentences.zh: 当一群人做到了他们本以为不可能的事，冲进国会大厅，在里面盘踞数小时，

sentences.en: and then leave, many of them, to post their videos and photographs online?
sentences.zh: 然后离开，其中许多人还把自己的视频和照片发到网上，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: They want to build on that momentum, and they're currently trying to figure out what the best way is to grow their cause,
sentences.zh: 他们想利用这种势头，目前正试图找出壮大其事业的最佳途径，

sentences.en: which is really to see Donald Trump serve another term in office, to see in their minds the rightful president assume control of the government.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标实际上是让唐纳德·特朗普再任一届，在他们心中，是让合法的总统重新掌控政府。

sentences.en: So what does that actually look like in the wake of a physical attack that, as you said,
sentences.zh: 那么，在经历了一场正如你所说，

sentences.en: was in its own terrifying way successful, but has resulted in a tremendous online crackdown?
sentences.zh: 以其自身恐怖方式取得“成功”，但却导致了大规模网络打击的物理袭击之后，情况究竟如何？

sentences.en: So in the hours after the siege, you see a lot of these guys going on Twitter and Facebook, and they're posting celebratory images,
sentences.zh: 在围攻发生后的几个小时里，你会看到很多这样的人在推特和脸书上发布庆祝性的图片，

sentences.en: showing how awesome they look as the Speaker of the House, or roaming the halls of Congress, and they're clearly really excited about what they've done.
sentences.zh: 展示他们坐在众议院议长座位上或在国会大厅游荡时看起来有多“威风”，他们显然对自己的所作所为感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: But by the next morning, some of these accounts start to disappear.
sentences.zh: 但到了第二天早上，其中一些账号开始消失了。

sentences.en: Overnight, Twitter announced it perched more than 70,000 accounts associated with QAnon content.
sentences.zh: 一夜之间，推特宣布封禁了超过7万个与“匿名者Q”（QAnon）内容相关的账号。

sentences.en: At first, they're just taking down photos and videos on places like Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们只是在脸书和推特等平台上删除照片和视频。

sentences.en: Facebook, meantime, saying today they've removed over 600 militarized social movements.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，脸书今天表示他们已经移除了超过600个军事化社会运动组织。

sentences.en: President Donald Trump has found himself effectively deplatformed.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统发现自己实际上已被剥夺了平台。

sentences.en: Around this time, Trump himself is knocked off one social media platform after another.
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时候，特朗普本人被一个又一个社交媒体平台封杀。

sentences.en: From Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and Twitch.
sentences.zh: 从脸书、Instagram、YouTube到Twitch。

sentences.en: And then whole groups, Twitter accounts with tens of thousands of followers, realize they've gone too far,
sentences.zh: 接着，整个群体，那些拥有数万粉丝的推特账号，意识到他们做得太过火了，

sentences.en: and that social media isn't going to allow them to post these overtly violent images online.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体不会允许他们在网上发布这些公然暴力的图像。

sentences.en: And they start to migrate to more fringe places like Gab and Parler.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始向Gab和Parler等更边缘的平台迁移。

sentences.en: The niche social platform Parler, which has drawn conservatives as well as far-right extremists, saw a surge in downloads, rising to number one in Apple's App Store.
sentences.zh: 小众社交平台Parler吸引了保守派和极右翼极端分子，其下载量激增，一度跃升至苹果应用商店榜首。

sentences.en: And so they think Parler is going to be the answer.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为Parler会是答案。

sentences.en: They think President Trump is going to join them there.
sentences.zh: 他们认为特朗普总统会加入他们。

sentences.en: Then this morning, Parler went dark after losing access to Amazon Web Services, which hosts the content.
sentences.zh: 然而今天早上，在失去亚马逊网络服务（AWS）的托管支持后，Parler陷入瘫痪。

sentences.en: Within a day, they find that that's taken down as well.
sentences.zh: 不到一天，他们发现那个平台也被拿下了。

sentences.en: It was being hosted by Amazon, Amazon very quickly pulled the plug, and all of a sudden, Parler is inaccessible.
sentences.zh: 它原本由亚马逊托管，亚马逊很快就切断了服务，突然之间，Parler就无法访问了。

sentences.en: And so in a matter of days, they find themselves booted not just off of Twitter and Facebook, but now off Parler and Gab, which is one of the only sites sort of online remaining,
sentences.zh: 所以在短短几天内，他们发现自己不仅被踢出了推特和脸书，现在连Parler和Gab也被封了，而Gab是网上仅存的几个平台之一，

sentences.en: is so flooded with requests by new users that it's just unbearably slow.
sentences.zh: 因为涌入的新用户请求太多，导致速度慢得令人无法忍受。

sentences.en: It takes minutes, sometimes five, six minutes to load a single page on Gab.
sentences.zh: 在Gab上加载一个页面有时需要几分钟，甚至五六分钟。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it's basically just overclogged with right-wing conservatives who have been booted off these other platforms?
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上是被那些从其他平台被踢出来的右翼保守派给挤爆了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Gab becomes, if you remember the days of dial-up internet, where you would just kind of sit and watch a page load for minutes at a time, that's what Gab starts to feel like.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得拨号上网的年代，那种坐在电脑前看着页面加载几分钟的感觉，Gab现在就是那种体验。

sentences.en: And so they realize that they have to move elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 于是他们意识到必须转移到别处。

sentences.en: And this idea builds that, why don't they go to the encrypted parts of the web, to apps that have already been around for a long time, like Telegram and Signal,
sentences.zh: 于是产生了一个想法：为什么不去网络上加密的部分，去那些早就存在已久的应用程序，比如Telegram和Signal，

sentences.en: and build a following there.
sentences.zh: 并在那里建立粉丝群呢？

sentences.en: And it happened so quick.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切发生得非常快。

sentences.en: I was in one group for the Proud Boys, which is a far right-wing militia.
sentences.zh: 我加入了一个“骄傲男孩”（Proud Boys）的群组，这是一个极右翼民兵组织。

sentences.en: I watched them grow 8,000 members in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 我看着他们在几天内增加了8000名成员。

sentences.en: And what are you seeing happening in these encrypted platforms, in the Signals,
sentences.zh: 在这些加密平台，在Signal和Telegram上，随着所有这些保守派活动人士、煽动者和策划者涌入，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: and the Telegrams, as all these conservative activists and agitators and plotters are now flooding in?
sentences.zh: 如果你把网络想象成一个巨大的球体，

sentences.en: So if you imagine the web as like, you know, as this one big ball,
sentences.zh: 表面上是脸书、推特以及你和你的朋友、家人常去的地方，

sentences.en: and on the surface of it you have Facebook and Twitter and all the places that you and your friends and your family hang out,
sentences.zh: 再往深一层，也许有Parler和Gab，虽然不太出名，但任何人都可以加入。

sentences.en: and then you go one layer deeper and maybe there's Parler and Gab, which, I don't know, they're less known, but anybody can join them really.
sentences.zh: 再深一层，就是Telegram和Signal这样的应用。

sentences.en: One layer deeper than that, you have the apps like Telegram and Signal.
sentences.zh: 它们更难被发现。

sentences.en: They're harder to find.
sentences.zh: 你必须确切地知道自己在找什么。

sentences.en: You have to know exactly what you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 你必须主动加入。

sentences.en: You have to join.
sentences.zh: 它们会被各种消息、内部代码和术语淹没。

sentences.en: They can be inundated by messages and internal codes and language.
sentences.zh: 你必须真的想去那里才能加入。

sentences.en: And you have to really know that you want to be there in order to join.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们到达那里时，他们突然成为了这个核心圈子和内部群体的一部分，在那里什么都可以说。

sentences.en: So when people get there, they suddenly become part of this inner circle and this inner group where anything goes.
sentences.zh: 这是一个加密频道。

sentences.en: It's an encrypted channel.
sentences.zh: 你可以说任何你想说的话。

sentences.en: You can say whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 你可以认为执法部门无法追踪到你。

sentences.en: You can assume that law enforcement will not be able to trace it back to you.
sentences.zh: 你会感觉自己身处一个小而封闭的社区，里面都是志同道合的人，他们和你有着相同的信仰，想要同样的东西。

sentences.en: And you feel like you're in this like small cloistered community of like-minded individuals who believe the same things you do and who want the same things you want.
sentences.zh: 于是他们的语言、他们的言论变得一天比一天极端。

sentences.en: And so their language, their rhetoric just becomes day after day more extreme.
sentences.zh: 他们开始将自己视为真正的信徒，特朗普真正的战士，被主流平台踢出、封禁和噤声，

sentences.en: They start to see themselves as the true believers, the true soldiers of Trump, who have been kicked off and banned and silenced by the mainstream platforms
sentences.zh: 现在找到了通往这些加密频道的路，在那里他们可以策划他们所说的“真正的革命”。

sentences.en: and have now found their way to these encrypted channels where they can plan what they say is real revolution.
sentences.zh: 那么，自1月6日以来，他们的策划性质以及这种充满怨恨、或许还有些胆大妄为的对话是什么样的？

sentences.en: And so what is the nature of their planning and of this embittered and maybe somewhat emboldened conversation in the days since January 6th?
sentences.zh: 目前，我在Telegram和Signal上关注着几十个民兵组织。

sentences.en: At this point, there are several dozen militia groups on Telegram and Signal that I'm following.
sentences.zh: 我正在观察他们的计划，但说实话，他们毫无章法。

sentences.en: And I'm watching their plans, but really, they're all over the map.
sentences.zh: 有些人想在1月16日发起一场针对华盛顿特区国会大厦的游行。

sentences.en: Some of them want to see a march on the Capitol, on Washington, D.C., starting on January 16th.
sentences.zh: 其他人则在谈论在全美50个州的首府同时游行。

sentences.en: Others are talking about marching on all 50 U.S.
sentences.zh: 在这些对话的潜台词中，他们会说类似“请自行决定是否携带武器”的话。

sentences.en: capitals.
sentences.zh: 很明显，那里确实存在暴力机会和潜力。

sentences.en: And in the subtext of those conversations, they're saying things like, come armed at your own discretion.
sentences.zh: 他们还讨论了在谷歌、推特和脸书等科技公司门前进行抗议的计划。

sentences.en: And so it's clear that there's a real opportunity and potential for violence there.
sentences.zh: 我还看到有人呼吁对从《纽约时报》到CNN和《华盛顿邮报》等新闻机构采取行动。

sentences.en: They've also talked about efforts to have protests in front of tech companies like Google, Twitter, and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上还在决定下一步要做什么。

sentences.en: And I've seen calls for actions against news organizations ranging from the New York Times to CNN and the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 我想问一下，我得小心一点，因为我不想以任何方式美化或宣传这一点，

sentences.en: So they're really still making up their mind on what they want to do next.
sentences.zh: 但从这些交流中，你能读出什么有启发性的东西吗？

sentences.en: I wonder, and I want to be careful here because I don't want to romanticize this in any way or promote it,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，昨晚我看到的一段交流很能说明他们的策划水平，

sentences.en: but is there anything you can read from some of these exchanges that feels illuminating?
sentences.zh: 以及他们思考问题的方式，那是两个民兵组织成员之间的对话，他们想跨州旅行。

sentences.en: In my mind, one of the exchanges I saw last night that I thought was sort of telling about their level of planning
sentences.zh: 他们想去州议会大厦游行，他们一直在讨论跨州携带什么武器是合法的。

sentences.en: and the way they think about this was between two members in one militia group who wanted to travel across state lines.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在搜索当地法律，说，好吧，在这个州，某种武器是合法的。

sentences.en: They wanted to march on a capitol, a state capitol building, and they were going back and forth among themselves about what arms could they legally carry across state lines.
sentences.zh: 在那个州，又是另一种武器。

sentences.en: And so they're searching through local laws to say, right, well, in this state, such and such a weapon is legal.
sentences.zh: 如果我们跨州运输它，被公路巡警拦下，我们会不会有麻烦？

sentences.en: In that state, it's this other weapon.
sentences.zh: 他们不是业余爱好者。

sentences.en: If we transport it across state lines and we get stopped by a highway patrolman, are we in trouble?
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种感觉是他们不知道自己在做什么，或者他们是在即兴发挥。

sentences.en: They're not amateurs.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I think there's this sense that they don't know what they're doing or that they're acting off the cuff.
sentences.zh: 在其中一些组织中，确实存在非常严肃的策划。

sentences.en: And that isn't the case.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: By some of these groups, there is very serious planning happening.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的让我想起了你说在1月6日之前看到的那些策划，

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 关于什么东西可以带上飞往华盛顿的飞机，如何隐藏它，这些相当详细的讨论。

sentences.en: What you're describing reminds me of the planning that you said you saw before January 6th,
sentences.zh: 在纸面上听起来很离谱，直到你意识到那些策划确实发生了，并导致了这次对国会大厦的袭击。

sentences.en: this rather detailed discussion of what could be brought on a plane to Washington, how it could be hidden.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it sounds pretty far-fetched on the page until you realize that that planning happened and it resulted in this assault on the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的正是同样的讨论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我唯一要指出的是，他们现在还在犹豫是否要付诸行动。

sentences.en: And we're seeing exactly that same discussion.
sentences.zh: 他们正在为此做计划。

sentences.en: The only difference I would note now is that they're still on the fence about whether or not they're going to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们正在设定不同的日期。

sentences.en: They're planning for this.
sentences.zh: 他们在说，我们应该在16号行动吗？

sentences.en: They're casting kind of different dates.
sentences.zh: 我们应该在19号去吗？

sentences.en: They're saying, should we do it on the 16th?
sentences.zh: 我们是不是应该等到20号？

sentences.en: Should we go on the 19th?
sentences.zh: 我认为这种困惑很大程度上是因为直到现在，他们一直认为自己是在听从特朗普总统的指令。

sentences.en: Should we maybe wait until the 20th?
sentences.zh: 当特朗普发推文说1月6日是关键的一天，国会批准投票结果是关键时刻时，

sentences.en: And I think a lot of that confusion is because until now, they have seen themselves as taking their marching orders from President Trump.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这就是他们需要的信号，表明那是前往国会大厦的日子。

sentences.en: When Trump tweeted that January 6th was a key day, that Congress ratifying the votes was a key moment,
sentences.zh: 现在，在他们认为得到了总统的“认可”之后，他们一直在争论接下来该做什么。

sentences.en: that for them was the sign they needed that that was the day to come to the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来他们这次没有明确的命令，也没有真正明确的领导层。

sentences.en: Right now, in the wake of what I think in their minds is a sign-off from the president, they have been arguing among themselves about what they should do next.
sentences.zh: 是的，有趣的是，我很好奇，我想人们未来几年都会研究这种影响，因为当他们被踢出脸书和推特等平台时，

sentences.en: So they have no clear orders this time and they have no real clear leadership, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 也剥夺了这些组织相互观察、透明交流以及了解他人计划的能力。

sentences.en: Yeah, and what's interesting, I'm curious, I think people will be studying the effects of this for years to come because when they were booted off places like Facebook and Twitter,
sentences.zh: 现在随着他们变得四分五裂，你看到了各种分散的努力，他们正在挣扎。

sentences.en: they also took away the ability for these groups to kind of see one another and transparently talk and see what the others were planning.
sentences.zh: 昨天早上有一段对话，其中一个人说，

sentences.en: And now as they become fractured, you see these kind of disparate efforts happening and they're struggling.
sentences.zh: 我太困惑了，直接告诉我该做什么吧。

sentences.en: There was a conversation yesterday morning where one of them said,
sentences.zh: 你们想让我16号去华盛顿吗？

sentences.en: I'm so confused, just tell me what to do already.
sentences.zh: 你们想让我17号去弗吉尼亚吗？

sentences.en: Do you want me to come to Washington on the 16th?
sentences.zh: 我需要知道我的车要加多少油，我需要储备燃料。

sentences.en: Do you want me to go to Virginia on the 17th?
sentences.zh: 他非常沮丧，因为他觉得没有得到以前在脸书和推特等中心化平台上那种明确的指令。

sentences.en: I need to know how much gas I've got to put in my car and I need fuel reserves.
sentences.zh: 感觉这些组织的去平台化，即我们在1月6日之后的几天里看到的网络打击，让所有这些人变得组织性更差了，

sentences.en: And he was really frustrated because he felt like he wasn't getting the clear orders that he used to get from centralized groups in places like Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: 因为他们被分散到了这些加密服务中。

sentences.en: It feels like the deplatforming of these groups, the online crackdown we have seen over the past few days since January 6th, has left all of these people less organized
sentences.zh: 但这是否意味着参与其中的人变少了？

sentences.en: because of the way that they've been spread out across these encrypted services.
sentences.zh: 还是说这根本无法得知？

sentences.en: But does that mean there are fewer of them engaged in this?
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们知道参与的人是否变少了。

sentences.en: Or is that not really knowable?
sentences.zh: 他们绝对是在试图吸引更多的人。

sentences.en: I don't think we know if there are fewer engaged.
sentences.zh: 我认为一些民兵组织的领导人现在非常担心，他们无法像在推特和脸书上那样吸引新追随者了。

sentences.en: They're definitely trying to attract more people.
sentences.zh: 他们需要新追随者才能生存。

sentences.en: I think that the leaders of some of these militias are really worried right now that they won't be able to attract new followers in the same way that they could
sentences.zh: 他们需要人们不断地加入他们的运动。

sentences.en: when they can post on Twitter and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以我观察到本周早些时候发生了一件有趣的事，当时有人讨论如何将“匿名者Q”阴谋论运动的人吸引到民兵组织中。

sentences.en: And they need new followers to survive.
sentences.zh: 当然，1月6日的集会上有很多“匿名者Q”的支持者。

sentences.en: They need people to be constantly coming into their movement.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人参与了骚乱并冲击了国会大厦。

sentences.en: So I watched this interesting thing happen earlier this week where there was a discussion on how to attract people from QAnon, the conspiracy movement, into militias.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于一些民兵组织来说，他们看到了一个成熟的受众群体，可能有成千上万相信“匿名者Q”阴谋论的美国人，

sentences.en: Of course, there were many QAnon supporters at the rally on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 他们现在可能正处于沮丧之中，愿意加入民兵组织，并对他们多年来一直相信的那些阴谋论采取实际行动。

sentences.en: Some of them rioted and stormed the Capitol building.
sentences.zh: 那么，这些组织者正在做什么来试图招募“匿名者Q”的成员和支持者呢？

sentences.en: And so for some of these militias, they see this kind of ripe audience of potentially hundreds of thousands of Americans who believe in the QAnon conspiracy,
sentences.zh: 他们正在自觉地采用许多“匿名者Q”的语言，即世界是由深层政府阴谋集团控制的，他们正在秘密地收割幼童，

sentences.en: who might be willing right now in a point of frustration to join militias and actually take action on some of those conspiracies that they've been believing for years now.
sentences.zh: 贩卖幼童，如果人们加入民兵组织，就可以对抗这一切。

sentences.en: And so what are these organizers doing to try to recruit members of QAnon, supporters of QAnon, this baseless conspiracy?
sentences.zh: 他们试图通过在网上尽可能多地发布数字版的“名片”来将他们拉入民兵组织。

sentences.en: They're self-consciously adopting a lot of the QAnon language that the world is run by this deep state cabal and that they are secretly harvesting young children,
sentences.zh: 他们会说，到处关注我，因为我们不知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: trafficking in young children, and that if people join militias, they can fight that.
sentences.zh: 一旦你在那里关注了他们，一旦你进入了他们的加密Telegram频道或Signal，他们就会给你六七个备用账号让你关注，

sentences.en: And they're trying to draw them into their militias by putting online the digital equivalent of a calling card everywhere they can.
sentences.zh: 以防其中一个被封，因为他们知道其中一些很可能会被封掉。

sentences.en: And they would say, follow me everywhere because we don't know what's going to come down next.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And then once you follow them there, once you're on their encrypted telegram channel or signal, they then give you six or seven alternate accounts to follow
sentences.zh: 希拉，这些领导人的适应能力之强，以及他们为下一次打击所做的准备之充分，让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: just in case that one gets taken down because they know that it's very likely that some of these will get taken down.
sentences.zh: 感觉这些打击只会促使他们扩大自己认为需要存在的平台数量。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I'm struck, Shira, by just how adaptable the leaders of this are, by how much they are planning for the next crackdown.
sentences.zh: 希拉，这些领导人的适应能力之强，以及他们为下一次打击所做的准备之充分，让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: And it feels like the crackdowns are just leading them to broaden the number of places that they think they need to be.
sentences.zh: 感觉这些打击只会促使他们扩大自己认为需要存在的平台数量。

sentences.en: It's not really stopping them.
sentences.zh: 这并不能真正阻止他们。

sentences.en: They're planning for a long-term war.
sentences.zh: 他们正在为一场长期战争做准备。

sentences.en: And these are people who are digital natives.
sentences.zh: 而且这些人都是数字原住民。

sentences.en: They have grown up on the internet.
sentences.zh: 他们是在互联网上成长起来的。

sentences.en: A lot of them formed these communities when they were teenagers.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人在青少年时期就形成了这些社区。

sentences.en: And so being very online and very flexible about how they are online is just part of their DNA.
sentences.zh: 因此，非常依赖网络，并且在如何使用网络方面非常灵活，这已成为他们基因的一部分。

sentences.en: It's part of how they think about the world.
sentences.zh: 这是他们思考世界方式的一部分。

sentences.en: They know they need that in order to be successful.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，要想成功，就需要这一点。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Shira, a very important question would seem to be, has this crackdown that you just described as sending these organizers of January 6th
sentences.zh: 那么，希拉，一个非常重要的问题似乎是，你刚才描述的这种镇压行动，是否将这些1月6日的组织者

sentences.en: off into many of the darkest corners of the internet, has that made it harder for law enforcement to do its job, which is to monitor their planning,
sentences.zh: 赶到了互联网上许多最黑暗的角落，这是否让执法部门更难开展工作，即监控他们的计划、

sentences.en: their discussions, their thinking?
sentences.zh: 他们的讨论和他们的想法？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: As these groups become fractured and spread, not just to different parts of the web, but also to different channels within each app that they're using,
sentences.zh: 随着这些团体变得四分五裂并扩散开来，不仅是到了网络的不同部分，还到了他们所使用的每个应用程序内的不同频道，

sentences.en: that is that many more places that law enforcement have to constantly be monitoring.
sentences.zh: 这意味着执法部门需要持续监控的地方更多了。

sentences.en: I spend hours of my day looking at these telegram and signal channels, and even I find it hard to keep up with the pace of communication in some of these networks.
sentences.zh: 我每天花几个小时查看这些Telegram和Signal频道，连我都觉得很难跟上其中一些网络中交流的速度。

sentences.en: There was one group I was in this morning, a QAnon group, which I think I counted close to 400 messages in the span of an hour.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我所在的其中一个群组，是一个匿名者Q（QAnon）群组，我想我在一小时内数了近400条消息。

sentences.en: And if you're a law enforcement and you're trying to monitor and figure out if someone is really making a bomb threat or if another person's actually carrying a weapon,
sentences.zh: 如果你是执法人员，试图监控并弄清楚某人是否真的在发出炸弹威胁，或者另一个人是否真的携带了武器，

sentences.en: keeping up with the sheer volume has got to be really difficult.
sentences.zh: 跟上如此巨大的信息量肯定非常困难。

sentences.en: Is that to say that perhaps it was easier at all to monitor these groups when everyone understood that they were congregating in one or two places?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着，当大家都知道他们聚集在一两个地方时，监控这些团体或许会更容易一些？

sentences.en: For example, a parlor, which felt like a hotbed in the past couple of months.
sentences.zh: 例如，Parler，在过去几个月里感觉就像一个温床。

sentences.en: I spoke to someone from the FBI a couple days ago who has been tracing far-right groups for the last decade or so.
sentences.zh: 几天前，我与一位联邦调查局（FBI）的人谈过，他追踪极右翼团体已经有十年左右了。

sentences.en: And the way he described it is actually much like we think of it as reporters, which is what you saw on Twitter and Facebook was just the surface level,
sentences.zh: 他描述的方式其实很像我们记者看待它的方式，即你在推特和脸书上看到的只是表面现象，

sentences.en: but it gave you clues to what they were thinking and what they were saying.
sentences.zh: 但它为你提供了他们想法和言论的线索。

sentences.en: And so if there was a new date that they were rallying around, like January 6th, for instance, you would see that trickle out to Facebook and to Twitter
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他们有一个新的集会日期，比如1月6日，你会看到消息流传到脸书和推特上，

sentences.en: and you would know what to look for in other places.
sentences.zh: 你就会知道在其他地方该寻找什么。

sentences.en: It was like they were leaving behind little breadcrumbs of what they were actually planning in some other places.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在其他地方留下了他们实际计划的小小面包屑一样。

sentences.en: And now that that's gone, it's that much harder for law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 而现在这一切消失了，这对执法部门来说要困难得多。

sentences.en: They have to be penetrating these groups at a much deeper level to be able to gain the same type of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他们必须更深入地渗透到这些团体中，才能获得同样的情报。

sentences.en: And these networks are end-to-end encrypted.
sentences.zh: 而且这些网络是端到端加密的。

sentences.en: So you have to be in them to see what's being said.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须身处其中才能看到他们在说什么。

sentences.en: But even once you're in them, tracing them back to a specific person is difficult.
sentences.zh: 但即使你进去了，要追踪到具体的人也很困难。

sentences.en: Most of these people are using burner phones.
sentences.zh: 这些人大多数都在使用一次性手机。

sentences.en: They're not using their real names.
sentences.zh: 他们没有使用真实姓名。

sentences.en: They are signing up for these accounts through ways that mask their identities.
sentences.zh: 他们通过掩盖身份的方式注册这些账户。

sentences.en: Now I'm going to note that these networks,
sentences.zh: 现在我要指出的是，这些网络，

sentences.en: Telegram, Signal, they've been around for years.
sentences.zh: Telegram和Signal，已经存在多年了。

sentences.en: Journalists use them.
sentences.zh: 记者使用它们。

sentences.en: Human rights workers use them.
sentences.zh: 人权工作者使用它们。

sentences.en: They're incredibly important as a safe means to communicate.
sentences.zh: 它们作为安全的沟通手段非常重要。

sentences.en: But no one knows what to do when they start to get used for people planning for violence.
sentences.zh: 但当人们开始利用它们策划暴力活动时，没人知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: So what kind of hope do federal and local law enforcement have in really policing these encrypted channels that you were describing,
sentences.zh: 那么，联邦和地方执法部门在真正监管你所描述的这些加密频道方面有什么希望呢？

sentences.en: especially if I'm remembering what you said earlier, that many of the organizers are envisioning action in multiple state capitals?
sentences.zh: 特别是如果我没记错你之前所说的，许多组织者正在设想在多个州首府采取行动？

sentences.en: So part of the reason that the organizers are moving towards this approach of launching marches and protests in all 50 state capitals is that they really want to try
sentences.zh: 组织者转向这种在所有50个州首府发起游行和抗议的方法，部分原因在于他们真的想尽一切可能

sentences.en: and make it as hard as possible for local law enforcement to plan ahead and stop them.
sentences.zh: 让地方执法部门难以提前计划并阻止他们。

sentences.en: They know that the FBI and the Department of Homeland Security and local police officers have some expertise in tracking them online.
sentences.zh: 他们知道联邦调查局、国土安全部和当地警察在网上追踪他们方面有一些专业知识。

sentences.en: They know how to use Telegram.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何使用Telegram。

sentences.en: They know how to use Signal.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何使用Signal。

sentences.en: They've used them before in investigations.
sentences.zh: 他们在调查中曾使用过这些工具。

sentences.en: But imagine you're a local police officer in a state like Ohio or Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 但想象一下，如果你是俄亥俄州或宾夕法尼亚州的一名当地警察。

sentences.en: And you now have to follow dozens of Signal groups and perhaps hundreds of Telegram channels to figure out exactly what these militias are planning next.
sentences.zh: 你现在必须关注几十个Signal群组和数百个Telegram频道，才能弄清楚这些民兵组织下一步到底在计划什么。

sentences.en: By dividing their efforts like this, they're really making it as hard as possible for law enforcement to decide what to do ahead of these rallies.
sentences.zh: 通过这样分散他们的行动，他们确实让执法部门在这些集会前难以决定该怎么做。

sentences.en: So that is the police side of this, Shira.
sentences.zh: 所以，希拉，那是警察方面的情况。

sentences.en: And now I want to turn for just a moment to the participants that you have been studying in these new dispersed channels.
sentences.zh: 现在我想花点时间谈谈你在这些新的分散频道中研究的参与者。

sentences.en: And whether you think that they see themselves as more capable and determined of future violence,
sentences.zh: 你是否认为他们认为自己更有能力、更有决心实施未来的暴力活动？

sentences.en: knowing that they were, and this is a weird word to use, but successful on January 6th, do they feel emboldened?
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道他们——用这个词可能有点奇怪——在1月6日成功了，他们感到胆量倍增了吗？

sentences.en: Did being able to get inside the Capitol make them think that they can do it again and that they should try to do it again based on what you're seeing?
sentences.zh: 能够进入国会大厦是否让他们认为自己可以再次做到，并且根据你的观察，他们应该尝试再次这样做？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Among the most fringe and extreme militia groups that exist here in the United States, there is absolutely a feeling that they have been emboldened by their success on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 在美国现存最边缘、最极端的民兵组织中，绝对有一种感觉，那就是他们在1月6日的成功让他们胆量倍增。

sentences.en: It was successful beyond their wildest dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 这比他们最疯狂的梦想还要成功。

sentences.en: And they see those optics of them not just entering the Capitol, but then leaving as a great recruiting tool.
sentences.zh: 他们将不仅进入国会大厦，而且还能全身而退的景象视为一种伟大的招募工具。

sentences.en: Some of that, I will say, just the tiniest bit has been mitigated by the arrest of some of those rioters in the week following January 6th.
sentences.zh: 我得说，其中一些影响在1月6日之后的一周内，由于一些暴徒被捕，已经得到了一丁点的缓解。

sentences.en: And as we've seen more arrests building, there have been more mentions in some of these private groups of, oh, wait, it looks like the FBI are actually getting serious
sentences.zh: 随着我们看到越来越多的逮捕行动，在一些私人群组中出现了更多关于“哦，等等，看起来联邦调查局真的动真格了”的讨论，

sentences.en: and cracking down on anyone who entered the Capitol building.
sentences.zh: 并且正在严厉打击任何进入国会大厦的人。

sentences.en: But it's an afterthought.
sentences.zh: 但这只是事后反思。

sentences.en: I mean, the vast majority of them think that they got away scot-free.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们绝大多数人认为自己逃脱了惩罚。

sentences.en: And now it's like, how much further can we go?
sentences.zh: 现在他们想的是，我们还能走多远？

sentences.en: What more will we be able to get away with?
sentences.zh: 我们还能逃脱什么样的惩罚？

sentences.en: And I have to imagine that the social media crackdown is in no way seen as real punishment.
sentences.zh: 而且我不得不认为，社交媒体的打击行动根本不被视为真正的惩罚。

sentences.en: Well, they were expecting
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们一直预料到

sentences.en: Facebook and Twitter to crack down on them.
sentences.zh: 脸书和推特会打击他们。

sentences.en: They have been talking about this for some time.
sentences.zh: 他们已经谈论这件事有一段时间了。

sentences.en: And again, we're talking about the most fringe kind of militia groups right now.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们现在谈论的是最边缘的那种民兵组织。

sentences.en: Among some of them, it's almost a badge of honor to get kicked off of Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: 在他们中间，被脸书和推特封号几乎是一种荣誉勋章。

sentences.en: It shows that you really got under their skin and that you were successful and that they had to get rid of you because you're just too powerful.
sentences.zh: 这表明你真的触动了他们的神经，你成功了，他们不得不除掉你，因为你太强大了。

sentences.en: And so you've seen a lot of boasting among some of these groups of, oh, well, I had 20 Facebook accounts and they shut down all 20 of them.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到这些团体中有很多吹嘘，比如“哦，我有20个脸书账号，他们把20个全封了”。

sentences.en: Aren't I, you know, all powerful that somewhere like Facebook had to shut down all my accounts and try and diminish my voice?
sentences.zh: 难道我不就是那种……你知道的，全能的人吗？以至于像脸书这样的地方不得不封掉我所有的账号，试图削弱我的声音？

sentences.en: There's this real sense of kind of
sentences.zh: 有一种真正的感觉，即

sentences.en: First Amendment rights being trampled on that is actually driving them to think even more boldly about what they can do on places like Telegram and Signal
sentences.zh: 第一修正案权利被践踏，这实际上驱使他们更胆大妄为地思考在Telegram和Signal这样的地方能做什么，

sentences.en: when they aren't being monitored and they're not scared of being shut down.
sentences.zh: 因为在那里他们不会被监控，也不怕被封杀。

sentences.en: So to return to where we began and given everything that you have told us,
sentences.zh: 那么回到我们开始的话题，鉴于你告诉我们的一切，

sentences.en: do you think at the end of the day that the crackdown that has followed
sentences.zh: 你认为归根结底，1月6日之后采取的打击行动，

sentences.en: January 6th
sentences.zh: 即1月6日事件，

sentences.en: taking these people off the well-known social media platforms and taking their champion,
sentences.zh: 将这些人从知名的社交媒体平台上移除，并将他们的领袖，

sentences.en: President Trump, off these platforms as well, has that made it more or less likely that in the coming days there's going to be more violence?
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统，也从这些平台上移除，这使得未来几天发生更多暴力的可能性是增加了还是减少了？

sentences.en: I think that they're in a moment of decision right now about what comes next this week.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们现在正处于决定本周接下来该做什么的时刻。

sentences.en: They haven't made up their minds.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有拿定主意。

sentences.en: Being on a private channel in some ways emboldens them to say whatever they want and to try to plan for the absolute sort of worst case scenarios.
sentences.zh: 身处私人频道在某种程度上让他们更有胆量去说任何想说的话，并尝试为绝对最坏的情况做计划。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, there's a ton of media attention on them right now.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，他们现在正受到大量的媒体关注。

sentences.en: They know the FBI and the police are watching them.
sentences.zh: 他们知道联邦调查局和警察正在盯着他们。

sentences.en: And so they could decide to bide their time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会决定静观其变。

sentences.en: And what do you mean bide their time?
sentences.zh: 你说的“静观其变”是什么意思？

sentences.en: In the short term, they're trying to figure out if they can actually stop
sentences.zh: 在短期内，他们正在试图弄清楚是否真的能阻止

sentences.en: Biden from becoming president and whether they can do something in the next week that allows Trump to assume office.
sentences.zh: 拜登就任总统，以及他们是否能在下周做些什么让特朗普能够就职。

sentences.en: A lot of them are saying that that's not possible.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人说这是不可能的。

sentences.en: They're kind of coming to the realization in this moment that what they planned on January 6th drew too much attention and that if they do anything in the next week,
sentences.zh: 他们此刻意识到，他们在1月6日的计划引起了太多的关注，如果他们在下周采取任何行动，

sentences.en: they're going to get arrested.
sentences.zh: 他们就会被捕。

sentences.en: And instead, they're taking a long-term view and they're saying we've attracted a lot of attention to our cause.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们正在采取长远的眼光，他们说我们已经为我们的事业吸引了很多关注。

sentences.en: We can recruit new members and come back in a year from now or two years from now and take everyone by surprise.
sentences.zh: 我们可以招募新成员，一年或两年后再回来，让所有人措手不及。

sentences.en: And now that they're on these encrypted channels, now that they have flocked to places like Telegram or Signal, they have found a place where they feel they can plan and recruit,
sentences.zh: 既然他们现在在这些加密频道上，既然他们已经涌向Telegram或Signal这样的地方，他们就找到了一个他们觉得可以策划和招募的地方，

sentences.en: which will, at some point in time, be away from the prying eyes of journalists and police and the FBI.
sentences.zh: 在某个时间点，这将远离记者、警察和联邦调查局的窥探。

sentences.en: And so you've really seen them embrace this kind of safe haven that they have created for themselves online.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实看到他们拥抱了这种他们在网上为自己创造的避风港，

sentences.en: which can become a real community for them going forward.
sentences.zh: 这可以成为他们未来真正的社区。

sentences.en: I mean, what you're describing, and it's pretty terrifying, is a kind of
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你所描述的，而且非常可怕，是一种

sentences.en: long-simmering rebellion.
sentences.zh: 长期酝酿的叛乱。

sentences.en: And from what you're saying, it may be, I don't know, but it may be too late to truly undermine it and rein it in.
sentences.zh: 从你的话来看，可能，我不知道，但可能已经太晚了，无法真正削弱它并加以控制。

sentences.en: I think these groups are here to stay.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些团体将长期存在。

sentences.en: And the thing is, if people were serious about stopping them, there would have been action taken four years ago when they were on places like Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: 问题是，如果人们真的想阻止他们，四年前当他们在脸书和推特上时就应该采取行动了。

sentences.en: That would have been the moment.
sentences.zh: 那才是最佳时机。

sentences.en: We're now four years later where they're so entrenched in their beliefs and they're now moving into a media ecosystem where they're in a small group where everyone agrees with them
sentences.zh: 现在四年过去了，他们对自己的信仰根深蒂固，而且他们现在正进入一个媒体生态系统，在那里他们处于一个小群体中，每个人都同意他们的观点，

sentences.en: and everyone holds the same extreme values.
sentences.zh: 每个人都持有相同的极端价值观。

sentences.en: Reaching them is going to be incredibly difficult.
sentences.zh: 接触他们将极其困难。
